newsitem.title: USA: World Bank head pledges support for ag research.
newsitem.headline: World Bank head pledges support for ag research.

text.p: World Bank president James Wolfensohn lauded the record of international agricultural researchers Monday and pledged the bank's support in future.

Wolfensohn spoke during a ceremony marking the 25th anniversary of the Consultative Group on International Agricultural Research, founded in 1971 with the bank's help. The group meets this week to discuss funding and direction of research.
Rice, wheat and corn varieties developed by CGIAR scientists help feed one billion people each day.
"I'm here to thank you for what you have done now and to pledge the bank's support in the future," he said.

Agricultural research offers the chance to increase food security and alleviate poverty, Wolfensohn said. But, for maximum benefit, it must be part of a "rural system" that allows crops to reach markets that are open to all.
"Seventy percent of our (the bank's) clients are in rural areas, the poor," Wolfensohn said, adding that 1.2 billion people have incomes of less than $1 a day.
It is rare for the World Bank president to address a CGIAR meeting.
